# Kael

> Native, GPU-accelerated application framework for building capable,
> resource-efficient desktop software in Rust. Kael 0.3 is a pre-1.0
> production candidate using Rust 1.97.1 and Rust 2024.

## Primary references

- Repository: https://github.com/Augani/kael
- Guide: https://augani.github.io/kael/
- Core API: https://docs.rs/kael
- Component API: https://docs.rs/kael_ui
- API documentation map: https://augani.github.io/kael/api-documentation.html
- Getting started: https://augani.github.io/kael/getting-started.html
- Core concepts: https://augani.github.io/kael/core-concepts.html
- Component library: https://augani.github.io/kael/component-library.html
- Platform APIs: https://augani.github.io/kael/platform-apis.html
- Capability bridge: https://augani.github.io/kael/native-capability-bridge.html

## Architecture

- `kael`: renderer, application runtime, entities, elements, styling, text,
  layout, input, accessibility, windows, and native platform primitives.
- `kael_ui`: optional, brandable component system built on `kael`.
- `kael` never depends on `kael_ui`.
- Focused `kael_*` crates provide storage, secrets, networking, documents,
  diagnostics, notifications, sharing, release, media, and engine services.
- WebView is an optional compatibility island, not the default UI model.

## Dependency choices

Core primitives:

```toml
[dependencies]
kael = "0.3"
```

Core plus ready-made components:

```toml
[dependencies]
kael = "0.3"
kael_ui = "0.3"
```

Lean Linux X11 build without WebView:

```toml
[dependencies]
kael = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["font-kit", "x11"] }
```

## Minimal application shape

```rust
use kael_ui::prelude::*;

struct AppView;

impl Render for AppView {
    fn render(&mut self, _: &mut Window, _: &mut Context<Self>) -> impl IntoElement {
        div()
            .size_full()
            .flex()
            .items_center()
            .justify_center()
            .child(Button::new("hello", "Hello, Kael!"))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    Application::try_new()?.run(|cx| {
        kael_ui::init(cx);
        install_theme(cx, Theme::dark());
        if let Err(error) = cx.open_window(WindowOptions::default(), |_, cx| {
            cx.new(|_| AppView)
        }) {
            eprintln!("failed to open window: {error}");
            cx.quit();
        }
    });
    Ok(())
}
```

## Working model

- Implement `Render` for application views.
- Store reactive state in `Entity<T>` values created with `cx.new`.
- Mutate entities with `entity.update(cx, |state, cx| { ... })` and call
  `cx.notify()` when the view must render again.
- Use `div()` and the `Styled` methods for primitive layout and appearance.
- Call `kael_ui::init(cx)` once when using the component crate.
- Read the active component theme with `Theme::of(cx)`.

## Platform accuracy rules

- Query `CapabilityReport::current()` for platform-dependent workflows.
- `Full` means a usable Kael backend exists.
- `Partial` and `RequiresInit` need an explicit setup/fallback path.
- `Unsupported` means an OS API or checked descriptor may exist, but Kael does
  not implement the native operation.
- `Disabled` means a required compile-time feature, such as `webview`, is off.
- A request builder validates intent; it is not proof of backend support.

Kael 0.3 does not provide native push registration, geolocation,
USB/HID/serial/Bluetooth discovery and I/O, native spellchecking, file-promise
drag sources, app-window snapshot backends, or share-receiver registration.
Do not generate code that claims these are complete.

## Source routing

- Core exports and module map: `crates/kael/src/kael.rs`
- Application/entity runtime: `crates/kael/src/app.rs`
- Elements: `crates/kael/src/elements/`
- Platform backends: `crates/kael/src/platform/`
- Capability truth table: `crates/kael/src/platform_caps.rs`
- Component exports: `crates/kael_ui/src/lib.rs` and `prelude.rs`
- Components: `crates/kael_ui/src/components/`, `display/`, `navigation/`,
  `overlays/`, and `charts/`
- Single repository-only showcase: `crates/kael_ui/examples/astryx_showcase.rs`

## Agent guidance

Prefer the smallest API that performs the requested operation. Do not introduce
a handoff, plan, manager, or abstraction for a one-step workflow. Preserve
fallible boundaries and platform errors. Use WebView only for an intentionally
web-owned surface. The optional `kael/agent-tools` feature contains structured
planning metadata, but agents can build applications directly from the public
Rust APIs without enabling it.
